title: Adding the ZSDK to an app: Android and iOS packages, prerequisites and sample apps

prose.text: The vendor publishes one public repository per platform. Each holds the install instructions and a sample app; the Android repository publishes the library as a package, and the iOS repository holds the binary itself. The API and the registration steps are in [[shared.zsdk.developer-api]] and [[shared.zsdk.configuration]].

checks.do: Whether the build can reach the GitHub Packages repository: a GitHub username and access token present as gpr.user and gpr.key or as the environment variables.
That the iOS deployment target is 15.0 or later before adding the package.
Which integration route the iOS app uses (SwiftPM, CocoaPods or manual), and for manual that the framework is set to Embed & Sign.

android-package.statement: The Android SDK is a Gradle dependency, `com.zscaler.sdk:zscalersdk-android:latest.release`, resolved from the GitHub Packages Maven repository `https://maven.pkg.github.com/zscaler/zscaler-sdk-android`, and the sample app builds against the floating `latest.release` version.

quotes: The sample app uses the latest version of the Zscaler SDK (latest.release). Update manually in build.gradle if required.

android-registry-credentials.statement: Fetching the Android SDK requires a GitHub username and access token: the README has gpr.user and gpr.key set in the global gradle.properties file at ~/.gradle/gradle.properties and falls back to the GITHUB_USERNAME and GITHUB_TOKEN environment variables, while the sample app reads those environment variables first and the gradle properties second.

quotes: Make sure gpr.user and gpr.key are set to your github username and access token in global gradle.properties file at ~/.gradle/gradle.properties
GitHub Personal Access Token**: Required for downloading the SDK.

android-sample-baseline.statement: The Android sample app is built with compileSdk 35, minSdk 28, targetSdk 35, the ABI filters armeabi-v7a and arm64-v8a (x86 and x86_64 excluded) and Gradle 8.10.2.

quotes: abiFilters += mutableSetOf<String>("armeabi-v7a" , "arm64-v8a") // Exclude x86 and x86_64

ios-install-paths.statement: The iOS SDK supports Swift Package Manager, CocoaPods and manual integration; manual integration adds the xcframework under Frameworks, Libraries, and Embedded Content with the embed option set to Embed & Sign.

quotes: ZscalerSDK iOS supports Swift Package Manager, Cocoapods, and manual integration.
In Frameworks, Libraries, and Embedded Content add `ZscalerSDK.xcframework`.

ios-minimum-version.statement: The iOS package declares iOS 15 as its minimum platform in both Package.swift and the podspec, and Package.swift needs swift-tools-version 5.9.

ios-prebuilt-binary.statement: The iOS SDK ships as a prebuilt binary, Zscaler.xcframework, which SwiftPM wraps as a binaryTarget and the podspec lists under vendored_frameworks; the podspec is version 5.0.0 with a Commercial licence type, and the xcframework carries an ios-arm64 device slice and an ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator slice.

sample-app-credentials.statement: Both sample apps need an App key and an Access Token entered, and the iOS sample builds through CocoaPods (platform iOS 15.0, with ZscalerSDK taken from the local repository path).

quotes: Ensure all required configurations (credentials - App key and Access Token) are added to the app while testing.
Make sure to add the App Key and Access Token.

android-sdk-requirements.title: Minimum Android version and ABIs the Android SDK itself supports
android-sdk-requirements.detail: The Android repository ships only the README and a sample app; minSdk 28 and the armeabi-v7a and arm64-v8a ABI filters are settings of the sample app. Nothing in the repository states what the SDK library requires.
android-sdk-requirements.blocks: answering whether an app with a lower minSdk or x86 builds can adopt the SDK

ios-manual-framework-name.title: Which xcframework name the manual iOS integration expects
ios-manual-framework-name.detail: The README's manual steps name ZscalerSDK.xcframework and a downloadable release zip, while the repository itself ships Zscaler.xcframework (referenced by Package.swift and the podspec). The repository has no release artifact to compare.
ios-manual-framework-name.blocks: following the manual integration steps literally
